solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Not close to Italian? On the contrary

blocks.note: something not close is distant from it
the usual abbreviation for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: Someone is told they are not near the Italian, and replies that the opposite is true.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hides that the first five words are a literal instruction: be far from the abbreviation for Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are emphatic denials used to reject what someone has just said as wholly wrong.

clue.text: Emergency service worker using axe on military aircraft

indicators.note: in a down clue one part sitting on another is written above it

blocks.note: to axe someone is to dismiss them
a combat plane

explanation.surface: A rescuer swings an axe at a warplane, perhaps to free a trapped pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: The axe looks like the rescuer's tool; it is the verb meaning sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Firefighters are the crews of the fire brigade, one of the blue-light services called out in a crisis.

clue.text: Mother entering stage school gets lead in Norma fast

indicators.note: one part goes into the middle of another, as a person enters a building
the lead of a word is the letter at its front
the first part acquires the next one, which is simply added on after it

blocks.note: the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art, a London drama school
an everyday word for mother
the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A mother joins a drama school and lands the title role in Bellini's opera Norma.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London. Fast is the noun, a period of going without food, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Muslim month of daylight fasting, so the whole month is a religious fast.

clue.text: Charge pounds for a badger-like creature

blocks.note: a rate is a price charged
L, from Latin libra, is the symbol for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A dealer quotes a price in pounds for an animal that looks like a badger.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is an African and Asian carnivore closely resembling the European badger in build.

clue.text: Batsmen hoping to do this adopt a determined attitude?

blocks.note: first meaning: in cricket two batsmen who build a long partnership together
second meaning: to refuse to give ground

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen that adds many runs; that is what the first half is describing.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to build a big batting partnership and to resist firmly, holding one's position against pressure.

clue.text: Attended to grooved surface round edges of tyre

indicators.note: one part goes round another, enclosing it
the edges of a word are its first and last letters

blocks.note: the patterned surface of a tyre that grips the road
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A mechanic inspects a tyre, attending to its grooved surface and its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyre is the British spelling of tire, the rubber on a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who treated a patient attended to them, giving them medical care.

clue.text: Attack report revealing credit arrangement

blocks.note: to charge is to rush at an enemy
an account is a description of events

explanation.surface: A report of an assault turns out to expose someone's credit dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge account at a shop lets a customer buy now and pay later, a form of credit.

clue.text: Wallpaper may have been put in one’s place

blocks.note: first meaning: literally trimmed to the right dimensions before hanging
second meaning: humbled, deflated

explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the idiom literally, as what a decorator does to a roll of paper; the second is its figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone cut down to size has had their self-importance deflated, which is what being put in one's place means.

clue.text: District Attorney up calling for confession

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for a US prosecutor
a vocation or sense of purpose

explanation.surface: A prosecutor stands up and calls for a defendant to confess.
explanation.walkthrough: A District Attorney is the American public prosecutor, abbreviated DA.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is a statement owning up to something, which is what a confession is.

clue.text: Naval vessel in attack, protecting peacekeepers? Bravo

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps round it as a shield

blocks.note: United Nations troops keep the peace
Bravo is B in the NATO alphabet
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A warship joins an assault while shielding peacekeeping troops, and someone cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: UN and B go between the G and O of GO AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunboat is a small armed warship, a vessel of a navy used mainly in coastal waters.

clue.text: Institute members came in as acid thrown

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about and lands in disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Members of an institute arrive as someone hurls acid, a lab accident or an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Academicians are members of an academy or learned institute such as the Royal Academy.

clue.text: Governor‘s girl in prison

indicators.note: the person sits inside the jail, placed within it

blocks.note: can is slang for jail
a girl's name

explanation.surface: The governor's daughter is behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan was the governor or keeper of a castle, so the word names a kind of governor.

clue.text: Supplant head of union by surprise? Not half!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
only half of the word is kept, the rest dropped
one part stands by the other, placed right next to it

blocks.note: the opening letter
taken as written, then cut

explanation.surface: A union leader is ousted in a surprise move, and someone remarks that it was hardly a surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first four of the eight letters of SURPRISE stay. 'Not half!' sounds like the British exclamation for 'very much so'.
explanation.definitionFit: To usurp is to seize someone's position wrongfully, which is to supplant them.

clue.text: The staggering article about oxygen is speculative

indicators.note: something staggering lurches about unsteadily, so these letters lose their order
about also means round and about, so the extra letter is mixed in with the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A staggering article about oxygen turns out to be guesswork, a science piece that is all theory.
explanation.definitionFit: Theoretical claims rest on theory rather than proven fact, so they are speculative.

clue.text: Forward terms of reference

blocks.note: first meaning: as a verb, to send money or a matter on
second meaning: as a noun, the scope of a task

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one phrase, forward terms of reference, but it splits into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To remit payment is to send it on, and a committee's remit is the area it has been asked to deal with.

clue.text: Lifting problem?

blocks.note: surface reading: a bad back, trouble picking up heavy things
setter's reading: lifting is slang for stealing, so the problem is a compulsion to steal

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a gym or back injury; lifting here means shoplifting.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition is a compulsive urge to steal, so it is a disorder whose symptom is helping oneself to goods.

clue.text: Relish spring, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is heard rather than read, so the word goes by its sound

blocks.note: a spring is the source of a river; in a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound the same

explanation.surface: Someone is said to relish the spring season.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a tangy condiment served with food, so a sauce is one kind of relish.

clue.text: Revolutionary chess organisation all the players, men, backed after second of elections

indicators.note: only the second letter of the word that follows is used
turned to face backwards, so read from right to left
the letter is placed following the first part

blocks.note: FIDE is the World Chess Federation
the second letter of the word
the cast is every actor in a production
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Chess officials and players line up behind someone after an election count.
explanation.walkthrough: L comes after FIDE, then CAST and OR reversed. Other ranks (OR) is a standard cryptic sense of men.
explanation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution of 1959, making him the archetypal revolutionary.

clue.text: Retailer‘s son pulled apart guard

blocks.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
past tense of tear
a custodian or warden

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper's son grapples with a security guard and pulls him off.
explanation.definitionFit: A storekeeper runs a shop, chiefly in American usage, so he sells goods retail.

clue.text: Left one’s home, dated

blocks.note: first meaning: departed from the house
second meaning: no longer in fashion

explanation.walkthrough: Dated could suggest courting, but here it means old-fashioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has gone out has left their house, and a style that has gone out is no longer current.

clue.text: Worn out, comic producing play

indicators.note: something comic is clowning about, so these letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exhausted comedian is putting on a play.
explanation.definitionFit: Our Town is Thornton Wilder's 1938 drama set in a small New Hampshire town, a famous American play.

clue.text: One fills some of the time at work

definitions.text: One fills some of the time at work

blocks.clueFragment: One fills some of the time at work
blocks.note: surface reading: a worker who passes part of the working day doing something
setter's reading: fills means putting fillings into teeth

explanation.walkthrough: Fills looks like killing time; it is the dental verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairing cavities with fillings is a routine part of this professional's working day.

clue.text: I caught it sitting next to poorly criminal

indicators.note: the parts sit side by side, joined in a row

blocks.note: poorly means unwell
taken as written
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who catches a bug sitting beside a sick person blames the criminal who gave it to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law, so an illicit act is a criminal one.

clue.text: Concern about rival in case

indicators.note: one word goes about the other, surrounding it

blocks.note: care means worry or concern
as in nobody can touch her, meaning equal or rival

explanation.surface: A worry about a competitor arises in a legal case.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche was a paper case holding a charge of powder, and the word also names a scroll-shaped cartridge box.

clue.text: Film male and female in ditch coupling

indicators.note: the two letters are placed inside the trench-like word

blocks.note: a trench is a long ditch
the male pronoun
F is the abbreviation for female
a coupling joins two things

explanation.surface: A man and a woman are coupling in a ditch, a scene from a film.
explanation.definitionFit: The French Connection is William Friedkin's 1971 police thriller starring Gene Hackman, which won the Oscar for best picture.

clue.text: Operetta: top it in style

indicators.note: the first two words are put inside the third

blocks.note: élan is flair or panache
to cap is to top or outdo
taken as written

explanation.surface: A director urges the cast to outdo an operetta and do it in style.
explanation.definitionFit: El Capitan is John Philip Sousa's 1896 comic operetta, a light opera from the composer of marches.

clue.text: Rachel thrown under horse in North Wales town

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed around and lands in disorder
in a down clue being under means written below the other part

blocks.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rider called Rachel is thrown and ends up beneath her horse in a Welsh town.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlech is a small coastal town in Gwynedd, North Wales, famous for its castle.

clue.text: Top Italian novelist died in coastal area of Massachusetts

blocks.note: a cap goes on top
Umberto Eco, author of The Name of the Rose
D is the abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A leading Italian novelist died on holiday on the Massachusetts coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cape Cod is the hooked peninsula forming the south-eastern coast of Massachusetts, a seaside holiday region.

clue.text: Fabulous bird having origins in Russia or China

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A legendary bird is said to come from Russia or China.
explanation.walkthrough: Fabulous here means belonging to fable, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a gigantic mythical bird of Arabian legend, appearing in the tales of Sinbad.

clue.text: Member of the clergy in park by rocky hill

indicators.note: one part stands by the other, placed alongside it

blocks.note: the rec, short for recreation ground, is a British public park or playing field
a tor is a rocky outcrop on a hilltop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A vicar strolls in a park near a craggy hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rector is a Church of England priest in charge of a parish, so a member of the clergy.

clue.text: Performer appearing in Hobart is Tasmanian

indicators.note: the letters show up inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and into the next two

explanation.surface: An entertainer is playing in Hobart and is a local Tasmanian.
explanation.definitionFit: Artist is used for any entertainer or performer, as in a recording artist or variety artist.

clue.text: Change what one plays in casino and get ahead after being behind?

definitions.text: Change what one plays in casino

blocks.clueFragment: Change what one plays in casino
blocks.note: first meaning: literally, move on to other gaming tables
second meaning: reverse a situation to gain the upper hand

explanation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally, as a gambler switching tables; the second is the usual figurative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn the tables is to reverse one's position relative to an opponent, going from losing to winning.

clue.text: Hit black bird of prey in hollow

blocks.note: to punch is to hit
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a nocturnal hunting bird

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a dark raptor down in a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A punchbowl is also a bowl-shaped depression in hills, a natural hollow, such as the Devil's Punch Bowl in Surrey.

clue.text: Not so easy housing old compulsive collector

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside

blocks.note: comparative of hard, difficult
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: It is getting harder to house all the old things a compulsive collector keeps.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarder compulsively accumulates and keeps things, often far beyond any need for them.

clue.text: Allow daughter to interrupt acrobat, an artiste

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle of another

blocks.note: an acrobat who performs feats of balance
to let is to allow
D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent lets their daughter interrupt a circus acrobat's act.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancer in classical ballet is a stage performer, an artiste in the theatrical sense.

clue.text: Page writer inside saw in supplement

indicators.note: the first two parts are placed inside the next

blocks.note: a saw is an old saying
P is the abbreviation for page
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A page in a magazine supplement shows a writer at work with a saw.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw is the noun meaning proverb, not a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendage is something added on to a larger whole, so it supplements it.

clue.text: Goddess, British actress, in a work by Browning

blocks.note: Aurora is the Roman goddess of the dawn
Vivien Leigh, star of Gone with the Wind

explanation.surface: A British actress plays a goddess in a Browning piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora Leigh is Elizabeth Barrett Browning's 1856 verse novel, her best-known long poem.

clue.text: Better when Focke, perhaps, loses height

indicators.note: what is lost is dropped from the word

blocks.note: Henrich Focke, the German aviation pioneer, is one man with this first name
H is the abbreviation for height

explanation.surface: A German aircraft designer improves when his plane loses altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Henrich Focke co-founded the Focke-Wulf aircraft company; 'perhaps' shows he is one example of the name. Better is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrich something is to improve its quality, which is to better it.

clue.text: Lucky charm found in the old lady’s bed

blocks.note: the old lady is slang for one's mother, so her bed is MA'S
a small bed

explanation.surface: A lucky charm turns up in Mum's bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a person, animal or object kept to bring good luck, like a lucky charm.

clue.text: Method of painting intended, we hear, to depict nature

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the sound of the word counts

blocks.note: painting with pigments bound in egg yolk
intended means had in mind

explanation.surface: An artist chooses a painting technique meant to capture the natural world.
explanation.walkthrough: Nature means a person's character here, not the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's temperament is their basic disposition, their nature.

clue.text: Magic circle originally taken in with guile

indicators.note: the original of a word is its first letter
something taken in is held inside another

blocks.note: the opening letter
taken as written
craft is cunning

explanation.surface: A member of the Magic Circle is fooled by cunning.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is the British society of conjurors. Magic is the definition and 'circle' gives only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Witchcraft is the practice of magic, especially spells and sorcery.

clue.text: Rhubarb crumble

blocks.note: first meaning: rhubarb is British slang for nonsense
second meaning: to decay and fall apart

explanation.walkthrough: Rhubarb crumble is a British pudding; here the words are separate. Rhubarb is also slang for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot is talk of nonsense, and as a verb it means to decompose and break up.

clue.text: Record statement made by Walter Mitty?

annotation.answer: ALL I HAVE TO DO IS DREAM

blocks.note: first meaning: a 1958 hit single by the Everly Brothers
second meaning: what a fantasist might admit about himself

explanation.walkthrough: Walter Mitty is James Thurber's daydreamer who imagines a heroic life, so the song title suits him.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is an Everly Brothers hit record and also a fitting confession from a man who lives in his daydreams.

clue.text: Impressive person, girl, appearing in double bill, then tango

indicators.note: she appears inside, placed between the others
what follows is simply added next in line

blocks.note: AC is short for account, a bill, and doubled it gives two copies
a lass is a girl
Tango is T in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A girl stars in a theatre double bill and then dances a tango, impressively.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone described as a class act is outstanding and admirable, so very impressive.

clue.text: Clear leader in variety show

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter

blocks.note: the opening letter
to indicate is to show

explanation.surface: The star of a variety show steps clear of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To vindicate someone is to clear them of blame or suspicion.

clue.text: Lock of hair stuck inside covering letter

indicators.note: the letters are lodged within the words that follow

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A lock of someone's hair is found stuck in with a covering letter, a keepsake.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringlet is a long spiral curl of hair, a single lock.

clue.text: Caustic play on words fellow delivers

blocks.note: a joke exploiting double meanings
gent is short for gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A man delivers a cutting remark through wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent remark is sharply biting or caustic in the way a strong smell stings.

clue.text: Former German state – American in Paris confused

indicators.note: something confused is muddled, its letters out of order
one part sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
US for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: An American tourist in Paris is muddled about a vanished German state.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a powerful German kingdom that dominated the German Empire and was formally abolished in 1947.

clue.text: Huge film

blocks.note: first meaning: of gigantic size, like the Titans
second meaning: James Cameron's 1997 film

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a huge film, a blockbuster, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means enormous, from the Titans of myth, and it is also the title of Cameron's record-breaking movie.

clue.text: Boat clubs backed by authority

indicators.note: one part is supported by another coming straight after it

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
an oracle is an infallible authority

explanation.surface: A boat club is funded by a local authority.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round boat of wicker covered with hide, used in Wales and Ireland.

clue.text: Salute maiden seduced by Zeus for so long

blocks.note: to cheer is to greet with acclaim
Io was a priestess loved by Zeus, who turned her into a heifer

explanation.surface: Someone salutes a mythical maiden whom Zeus seduced, and bids farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a British informal farewell, like saying so long or goodbye.

clue.text: Gemstone is left in Bolivian city university, large one

indicators.note: two parts go inside the city name

blocks.note: La Paz, Bolivia's seat of government
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left
U is the abbreviation for university
L is the abbreviation for large
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A large gem is left at a university in La Paz.
explanation.walkthrough: IS and L go inside LA PAZ, after its P; then U, L and I follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapis lazuli is a deep blue semi-precious stone used in jewellery and ground for ultramarine pigment.

clue.text: Herbivore also kept by father

indicators.note: something kept by another is held inside it

blocks.note: an everyday word for father
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: Dad also keeps a plant-eating pet.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda lives almost entirely on bamboo, so it is a plant-eating animal.

clue.text: Scottish group in Arizona react badly about me being imprisoned

indicators.note: done badly, these letters come out in the wrong order
the prisoner is shut inside the other letters

blocks.note: AZ is the postal abbreviation for the state
taken as written
ca, short for circa, means about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scottish band on tour in Arizona reacts badly when one of them is arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: About usually signals a container or reversal; here it is circa, abbreviated ca, part of the mixed letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aztec Camera were a Scottish pop band led by Roddy Frame, known for the 1980s hit Somewhere in My Heart.

clue.text: A letter in Hebrew starts to amaze locals entering public house

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the three words
PH is the map abbreviation for public house, a pub

explanation.surface: Pub regulars are amazed when a Hebrew letter is found on the door.
explanation.walkthrough: Entering is not a container signal: it is the third word whose first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph opens the Hebrew alphabet, corresponding to alpha in Greek, so it is one character of that script.

clue.text: Brigadoon girl heading off round island’s ancient region

indicators.note: the head, the first letter, comes off
the shortened name goes round the next part

blocks.note: Fiona is the heroine of the musical Brigadoon
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: The heroine of Brigadoon sets off around an island's ancient territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionia was the ancient Greek region on the west coast of Asia Minor, now Turkey.

clue.text: Ordered cab to canals in Spanish region

indicators.note: the letters are put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tourist orders a taxi to the canals while holidaying in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Costa Blanca is the stretch of Mediterranean coast around Alicante, a Spanish holiday region.

clue.text: Strangely frightening eastern chain with no borders

indicators.note: without its borders a word loses its first and last letters

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
a series is a chain of linked things

explanation.surface: An unbroken eastern chain of mountains has a strange, frightening air.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is uncanny and unsettling, frightening in a strange, unexplained way.

clue.text: Courage needed with large waves: they cause grief

indicators.note: one part goes along with the other, placed beside it

blocks.note: heart means courage, as in take heart
breakers are big waves crashing on the shore

explanation.surface: Surfers need courage to face huge waves, which bring sorrow when things go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartbreakers are people who cause romantic grief by breaking others' hearts.

clue.text: Murderer that court set free

indicators.note: letters set free are released to fall into any order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A court acquits a killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutthroat is a murderer, literally one who kills by slitting throats.
